## Purpose

This SOP describes field procedures for collecting soil samples
intended for molecular analysis, including DNA extraction, PCR/ddPCR,
amplicon sequencing, and metagenomics. Soil microbial communities are
sensitive to temperature, moisture, and oxygen exposure, and nucleic
acids degrade rapidly in the absence of proper preservation. The
procedures in this SOP are designed to minimize DNA and RNA degradation
from the moment of collection through transport to the laboratory,
ensuring that molecular results accurately reflect the in situ
microbial community [@knight2018; @frostegard1999].

This SOP supplements the general soil sampling procedures in
[SOP-F400](SOP-F400-soil-sampling.qmd) with additional precautions
specific to molecular work.


## Scope

- **Applies to:** Field collection of soil and rhizosphere samples for
  DNA extraction ([SOP-L700](../lab_sops/SOP-L700-dna-extraction.qmd)),
  ddPCR ([SOP-L701](../lab_sops/SOP-L701-ddpcr-nitrogen-cycle-primers.qmd)),
  amplicon sequencing, metagenomics, and other molecular analyses
- **Does not apply to:** Soil sampling for chemical or physical
  analysis only (see [SOP-F400](SOP-F400-soil-sampling.qmd)); water
  eDNA sampling (see [SOP-F700](SOP-F700-edna-field-sampling.qmd));
  laboratory-side DNA extraction and processing
- **Location:** All EA Program field sites


## Responsibilities

| Role              | Responsibility                                          |
|:------------------|:--------------------------------------------------------|
| PI / Field Lead   | Approve sampling design; specify target depth and
                      replication                                          |
| Trained Personnel | Collect and preserve samples per this SOP               |
| New Students      | Complete training (including contamination awareness)
                      before participating in molecular sampling           |


## Definitions

- **Contamination (molecular soil sampling):** Introduction of
  exogenous DNA from other samples, the environment, or the
  researcher's own microbiome into a soil sample; prevented by sterile
  tool sterilization between samples, frequent glove changes, and use
  of field blanks [@frostegard1999].
- **Cryogenic freezing (flash-freezing):** Rapid cooling of a soil
  sample in liquid nitrogen (-196 °C) or on dry ice (-78 °C)
  immediately after collection; arrests microbial metabolism and
  nuclease activity; required for RNA work and recommended for optimal
  DNA preservation [@knight2018].
- **Dry ice (solid CO~2~):** Used for field flash-freezing at -78 °C;
  causes frostbite on direct skin contact; must be handled with
  insulated cryogenic gloves and transported in a vented or insulated
  container.
- **Field blank:** An empty sterile tube or bag opened and closed at
  the field site during sampling; processed through the full
  extraction and PCR workflow in the lab; detects airborne or handling
  contamination; any positive amplification in a field blank
  invalidates the associated samples unless concentrations fall below a
  pre-established threshold [@frostegard1999].
- **Flash-freezing:** See cryogenic freezing.
- **LifeGuard Soil Preservation Solution (Qiagen):** A commercially
  prepared stabilization reagent that arrests nucleic acid degradation
  at ambient temperature for up to 7 days; an alternative to
  cryogenic preservation when dry ice is unavailable; add to the
  sample immediately after collection, invert gently, and store at
  room temperature or on ice.
- **Microbial community composition:** The relative abundances of
  different microbial taxa (bacteria, archaea, fungi) in a soil
  sample; highly sensitive to sample handling time, temperature, and
  oxygen exposure; shifts within minutes of soil disturbance
  [@knight2018; @frostegard1999].
- **Nuclease:** An enzyme that degrades DNA or RNA; active in soil
  samples at ambient temperatures; inactivated by low temperature
  (< 4 °C), chemical preservatives (LifeGuard buffer, ethanol), or
  rapid freezing.
- **Rhizosphere:** The narrow zone of soil immediately surrounding
  plant roots; has a distinct microbial community influenced by root
  exudates; sampled by collecting soil adhering directly to roots
  after gentle removal from the surrounding bulk soil.
- **Sterile technique:** A set of aseptic practices that prevent
  contamination of molecular samples; in soil microbial sampling,
  these include autoclaving or 70% ethanol sterilization of all metal
  tools, use of single-use sterile tubes and gloves, and minimizing
  exposure time to air [@frostegard1999].
- **Time from extraction to preservation:** A critical metric for
  molecular soil samples; ideally less than 2 minutes from the moment
  soil is removed from the ground to placement in ice, dry ice, or
  preservative; longer times cause measurable shifts in microbial
  community composition [@knight2018].


## Safety and Hazards

::: {.callout-warning}
### Hazards

- **Biological:** Soil may contain pathogens. Wash hands thoroughly
  after handling. Treat all samples as potentially infectious.
- **Physical:** Repetitive strain from augering; standard field
  hazards (heat, ticks, uneven terrain).
- **Chemical:** Liquid nitrogen causes severe cryogenic burns. Dry ice
  causes frostbite on direct skin contact. Handle with insulated
  gloves.
:::

### Required PPE

- [ ] Nitrile gloves (change between samples)
- [ ] Closed-toed shoes or field boots
- [ ] Insulated cryogenic gloves (if using liquid nitrogen or dry ice)
- [ ] Safety glasses (if using liquid nitrogen)
- [ ] Sun protection (hat, sunscreen)

### Emergency Procedures

Refer to [SOP-F001 Field Safety](SOP-F001-field-safety.qmd). For
liquid nitrogen or dry ice burns, warm the affected area gently with
lukewarm water. Do not rub.


## Equipment and Materials

### Sampling Equipment

| Item                                  | Notes                                    |
|:--------------------------------------|:-----------------------------------------|
| Soil auger (bucket-type, stainless steel) | Autoclaved or ethanol-sterilized before each event |
| Stainless steel trowel or spatula     | Autoclaved or flame-sterilized           |
| Ethanol (70%) in spray bottle         | For field sterilization between samples  |
| Lighter or butane torch               | For flame-sterilizing metal tools        |
| DI water squeeze bottle               | For rinsing tools after ethanol sterilization |

### Sample Containers and Preservation

| Item                                  | Notes                                    |
|:--------------------------------------|:-----------------------------------------|
| Sterile 50 mL Falcon tubes or Whirl-Pak bags | Pre-labeled; one per sample       |
| Cooler with ice packs (4 °C)          | Minimum preservation for DNA samples     |
| Dry ice (solid CO~2~)                 | For flash-freezing at -78 °C; preferred for RNA work |
| Insulated container for dry ice       | Styrofoam cooler or dewar                |
| LifeGuard Soil Preservation Solution  | Optional; stabilizes DNA and RNA at ambient temperature for up to 7 days |
| Ziplock bags (gallon size)            | For double-bagging frozen samples        |


## Procedure

### Pre-Field Preparation

1. Autoclave or ethanol-sterilize all metal sampling tools. Wrap in
   aluminum foil after sterilization.
2. Pre-label all sample tubes or bags: project ID, site, sample
   number, date, depth.
3. If using LifeGuard, pre-aliquot approximately 5 mL per tube.
4. Pack the cooler. If using dry ice, load the insulated container.
5. Include at least one field blank tube per sampling event.

### Sampling Procedure

1. Navigate to the sampling location; record GPS coordinates.
2. Put on fresh nitrile gloves.
3. Sterilize the auger or trowel: spray with 70% ethanol, allow
   30 seconds air-dry, optionally flame. Rinse with DI water.
4. Clear surface litter without disturbing mineral soil.
5. Collect soil from the target depth (typically 0--15 cm). Avoid
   large roots and rocks.
6. Using the sterilized trowel, transfer approximately 2--5 g of soil
   directly into the sterile tube. Minimize handling time; do not
   homogenize in a bucket.

::: {.callout-important}
### Speed Matters
Minimize the time between coring and preservation. The soil should be
in the tube and on ice within 2 minutes of extraction. Prolonged
exposure to air and ambient temperature causes shifts in microbial
community composition and DNA degradation
[@frostegard1999; @knight2018].
:::

7. Immediately preserve:
   - **DNA only:** Place capped tube on ice (4 °C). Transport to
     lab within 6 hours or freeze at -20 °C.
   - **DNA and RNA:** Flash-freeze on dry ice or liquid nitrogen.
     Transfer to -80 °C freezer on return.
   - **LifeGuard:** Add 5 mL LifeGuard to the soil, cap, invert
     3 times, store at ambient temperature up to 7 days.
8. Record in the field notebook: sample ID, GPS, depth, soil
   temperature, preservation method, time of collection, and
   any deviations.

### Decontamination Between Samples

1. Spray tools with 70% ethanol; allow 30 seconds air-dry; optionally
   flame. Rinse with DI water.
2. Change nitrile gloves.
3. Between sites, decontaminate boots and waders per
   [SOP-F007](SOP-F007-field-decontamination.qmd).


## Sample Transport and Storage

| Preservation Method      | Field Storage        | Lab Storage                |
|:-------------------------|:---------------------|:---------------------------|
| Ice (4 °C)               | Cooler, ice packs    | Process within 24 h or freeze at -20 °C |
| Dry ice (-78 °C)         | Insulated cooler     | Transfer to -80 °C freezer immediately |
| Liquid nitrogen (-196 °C) | Dewar               | Transfer to -80 °C freezer immediately |
| LifeGuard buffer         | Ambient, up to 7 days | Extract within 7 days; or freeze at -20 °C |

Record storage location in the Freezer Inventory and in the lab
notebook per [SOP-L106](../lab_sops/SOP-L106-refrigerators-freezers.qmd).


## Quality Control

- Include at least one field blank per sampling event.
- Change gloves and sterilize tools between every sample.
- Record the time elapsed between soil extraction and preservation.
  Flag any sample with elapsed time > 5 minutes.
- Field blanks positive for target DNA invalidate the batch unless
  concentrations fall below the established threshold.
- Avoid sampling immediately after rainfall when soils are saturated.

## Training Record

Before collecting soil samples for molecular analysis independently,
personnel must:

1. Read this SOP, [SOP-F400](SOP-F400-soil-sampling.qmd), and
   [SOP-L700](../lab_sops/SOP-L700-dna-extraction.qmd) in full
2. Demonstrate sterile sampling technique (tool sterilization, glove
   changes, rapid transfer to preservative) during a supervised
   practice session
3. Successfully process a field blank with a negative extraction and
   PCR result
4. Be signed off by the PI or field lead
